doc.title: Terri Lyne Carrington interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: Skipping school music; playing with Rahsaan Roland Kirk
summary: She sat in with Clark Terry and Rahsaan Roland Kirk by age ten and had little interest in school programs; she recalls Rahsaan's blindness, basketball and a cranberry sandwich.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: What about public school? Did you get an opportunity to play in the public school system?

No. I wasn’t very interested in playing in school because growing up I started playing at seven and by the time I was ten I was sitting in with a lot of people when they came through, like Clark Terry and Rahsaan Roland Kirk was like one of the first people that I played with. And I think before I even started playing he got me shaking a tambourine on stage with him and I think saxophone — I played saxophone for a minute when I was five or six. And then the drums. So when I was playing with people like that I wasn’t so interested in going through the music program in elementary or junior or even high school.
I can imagine that. It kind of spoiled you I guess. What was it like, do you remember the experience with Rahsaan?

Well he died when I was still pretty young. I remember various things. It’s funny what things stick out in your mind. I remember asking him a lot of questions about being blind. Because I was young and it was curious to me. And that he would shoot baskets at somebody’s house, they had a basketball hoop in their backyard and they would tap the hoop with a key or something, a piece of metal, so he could hear where it was and he would shoot. I don’t remember how good he was or not, but just the fact that he was doing that was pretty incredible to me at the time. And I would watch him eat, you know, © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-

just small things that intrigued me. I don’t know why this stands out in my mind but I remember he was eating a turkey sandwich and I think it had like maybe it was shortly after Thanksgiving, and he had cranberry sauce inside of the sandwich. And I had never seen that before.

I see. It is interesting the things we remember, but I remember seeing him live a couple of times and one of the things I remember is just the way he would negotiate finding his instruments. And they’d be all around him. Or hanging around his neck. And that was interesting to watch.
